verdict.rationale: Sentry's source is publicly readable on GitHub, and users report reading it to understand advanced integrations and self-hosting it for free. However, community evidence says the license is the BSL, which makes it source-available rather than open-source, with only older versions or forks under an open license. Missing for 10: an OSI-approved open license on the current codebase, and first-party documentation of the license terms.
